about.title: Torrance Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Torrance sits at a crossroads of the South Bay. Hawthorne Boulevard runs the length of the city, Pacific Coast Highway cuts across its southern edge, Crenshaw Boulevard carries commuters north and south, and the 405 hems in the whole map. Those four corridors also account for the largest share of the city's reported collisions. In 2025, the most recent final year on record, Torrance logged 329 injury collisions, with 490 people hurt and 5 lives lost. Fridays between 3 and 5 p.m. show the highest concentration of reports. If one of those numbers now describes you, the days ahead can feel scattered: medical bills, a car in the shop, an adjuster leaving voicemails. LawProactive exists to take one task off that list. We are not a law firm. We are a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney who handles California car accident claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery. You tell us what happened; we make the introduction.

items.title: You Have Two Years, Sometimes Far Less
items.desc: California gives most car accident victims two years to file, but a claim against a city, county, or state agency can require notice within six months. Getting connected early keeps every option open.

items.title: Partial Fault Does Not End Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible on Crenshaw or PCH, you may still recover a share of your damages. There is also no statutory cap on compensation for pain and suffering in an ordinary car accident case.

items.title: No Recorded Statement, No Upfront Fees
items.desc: An attorney can speak to the other driver's insurer for you, so you are never pressured into a recorded statement that may be used against you. The attorneys in our network work on contingency, and our connection service costs nothing.

items.question: I was hit on the 405 in Torrance and the CHP took the report. Does that change who I file a claim with?
items.answer: Not really. Freeway collisions within Torrance are typically handled by the California Highway Patrol rather than Torrance Police, so your report will come from the CHP, but your claim still goes against the responsible driver's insurance. If a defective road condition or a government vehicle played a role, a shorter notice deadline may apply, which is one reason to speak with an attorney promptly.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are generally not required to give a recorded statement to the other party's insurer, and doing so before you understand your injuries can work against you. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that minimize the claim. An attorney can handle that communication so you can focus on treatment.

items.question: What should I save from the crash while I wait to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Keep every photo you took at the scene, the exchange of information, medical discharge papers, and receipts for anything you paid out of pocket. Note the names of any businesses along Hawthorne Boulevard or PCH that might have cameras facing the roadway, since footage is often overwritten within days. Write down your own account of what happened while it is fresh.
